notes: Reviewed against native crops, source comparison proofs, complete inventories and words. Rules preserve optical-size differences and distinguish ornamental extensions from the body.

rules.notes: Ordinary capital bodies and round overshoots; B comes from the wider 18-point optical cut.
Observed or reconstructed triangular entries rise above the nominal cap line.
Descending capital terminals, including the explicitly inferred K.
Raised entry spurs and descending terminals belong to the observed capital forms.
Observed Q has a descending diagonal tail.
Observed uncial W has a rounded body and a descending exit spur.
Observed lining figures retain optical-size width variation.
The 18-point figure 1 is shorter than the larger-size figures; the source confirms this optical difference.
Lowercase bodies retain raised n/m/r/v entries and optical-size differences.
Descending lowercase exit spurs are retained independently of the body height.
Observed d and reconstructed b share an entry spur and descending exit.
Observed Handy Book 24-point b has a short descending exit and a cap-height entry spur.
Observed and reconstructed ascenders preserve their raised entry tips.
Observed Handy Book 54-point f has a curled head around the ordinary cap height.
Observed dotted i and t are lower than the spurred h/k/l ascenders.
New j retains the source i dot height and an inferred descending hook.
Observed g/p and inferred q preserve their descenders and varying optical body heights.
Observed y has a deep diagonal descender from the 24-point cut.
